title: reforce-meta.json
description: A reforce starter's published bean graph. This schema is a deliberately loose approximation meant for editor completion: cross-field rules (provides must contain the bean's own id, runtimeExport.module must stay inside the package, coordinates must resolve) are not expressible here. parseStarterMeta from @reforce/starter-meta is the admission gate; schema.json only helps you type.

schemaVersion.description: Schema major. Single integer, no minor: a reader either knows this major or refuses the file. Readers keep the parsers of older majors around, so one compiler reads starters published against several majors.

requires.description: Capabilities the reader must understand. Unknown keys are ignored by readers, which is a disaster for keys whose absence silently changes wiring - those keys name a capability here so an older reader fails loudly instead of mis-wiring.

starterDeps.description: Other starter packages whose meta coordinates appear in this file. They must reach the application registry too.

symbols.description: The package's public symbol table: what a coordinate of the form <package>#<export> resolves to.

beans.description: The beans this starter contributes to an application's container.

coordinate.description: A symbol coordinate: "<package>#<export>" for packages that publish a meta, or "<package>:<package-relative path>#<export>" for contract packages that do not.

relativePath.description: A package-relative posix path: no leading slash, no drive letter, no empty segment, no "." or ".." segment.

symbol.description: One entry of the package's symbol table.

file.description: The published declaration file the symbol is anchored to.

subpaths.description: The exports subpaths the symbol is reachable from, e.g. [".", "./testing"].

bean.description: One bean. Only class construction semantics are supported: dependencies are constructor parameters, in order.

provides.description: Every contract this bean satisfies. Must contain the bean's own id.

defaultBean.description: This bean only wins when nothing else provides the contract. Absent means false, and an absent-but-meant-true value merely produces an ambiguity error rather than a wrong wiring, which is why it is not a `requires` capability.

role.description: "root" materializes the bean even when nothing depends on it. "demand" (the default) only materializes it when something asks.

source.description: Where the bean is declared. Diagnostics only - no consumer dereferences the span by byte, and omitting it just costs a location line. Optional because it is the field a hand-written meta gets wrong first and outgrows first.

dependency.description: One constructor parameter of a bean.

contract.description: The contract this parameter asks for.

open.description: The contract needs a provider from outside this package. Recomputed by the reader, so a wrong value here is harmless.

collection.description: The parameter is a readonly T[]: every candidate for the contract is injected, and zero candidates is legal. Absent means a single edge - which is why writing it requires the "collection" capability.

runtimeExport.description: Where the reader imports the bean class from at runtime.

module.description: An import specifier inside the own package: the package name or one of its subpaths.

export.description: The exported binding name at that specifier.

lifecycle.description: Container lifecycle hooks the bean class implements. Absent means neither.

sourceReference.description: A span in a package file. Zero-based line and character; offset is used for tie-breaking only.

position.description: A zero-based position. end must not be earlier than start.
